name: Healthy Cooking: Balance Without Blandness
description: Cook without losing nutrients: steaming, a balanced plate, good fats in the right amount, and dessert without added sugar.

skills.name: Steaming
skills.description: Gentle, moist heat that cooks vegetables through without leaching their nutrients into boiling water.

skills.name: The Balanced Plate
skills.description: Protein, vegetable and carbohydrate in the right proportions on the same plate, not eaten as three separate afterthoughts.

skills.name: Good Fat, Right Amount
skills.description: A drizzle of olive oil or a few slices of avocado does more for a dish than avoiding fat entirely.

skills.name: Sweet Without Added Sugar
skills.description: Ripe fruit, spice and time can build sweetness that doesn't come from a bag of sugar.

skills.name: One Tray, Whole Dinner
skills.description: A hot oven and a tray that isn't crowded: vegetables roast and caramelise instead of stewing in their own steam.

skills.name: Acid, Herb, Heat Instead of Salt
skills.description: Lemon, vinegar, herbs and spice give a dish the lift people reach for the salt cellar to find.

lessons.title: Cooking With Steam
lessons.description: Gentle heat that cooks vegetables through without boiling their nutrients away.

preparationSteps.title: Water below the basket, never touching
preparationSteps.description: The vegetables cook in steam, not boiling water — direct contact would leach out nutrients.

preparationSteps.title: Cut pieces to a similar size
preparationSteps.description: Even pieces steam through at the same time — an uneven cut leaves some raw and some mushy.

preparationSteps.title: Check early, not by the clock alone
preparationSteps.description: Pierce with a knife tip — tender but still with a little bite is the target.

questions.prompt: Why does steaming keep more nutrients in vegetables than boiling them?
options: Steam cooks faster than boiling water
The vegetables never touch the water directly, so nutrients don't leach out into it
Steaming uses less water overall
Steam is hotter than boiling water
questions.correctAnswer: The vegetables never touch the water directly, so nutrients don't leach out into it
questions.explanation: Boiling submerges vegetables in water that pulls water-soluble nutrients out. Steaming cooks them without that direct contact.
questions.explainWrong: Steam isn't hotter than boiling water and isn't necessarily faster — the real reason is that boiling submerges food in the water nutrients dissolve into, while steaming never lets that contact happen.

lessons.title: The Balanced Plate
lessons.description: Protein, vegetable and carbohydrate together on the plate, in the right proportions.

preparationSteps.title: Half the plate in vegetables
preparationSteps.description: The largest portion should be vegetables — not an afterthought pushed to one side.

preparationSteps.title: A palm-sized portion of protein
preparationSteps.description: Enough to feel satisfying, without dominating the plate.

preparationSteps.title: A modest portion of carbohydrate
preparationSteps.description: A cupped handful of rice or grain rounds the plate out without overwhelming it.

questions.prompt: Which plate best follows the balanced-plate idea?
options: Mostly rice, a small side of chicken, no vegetables
Half vegetables, a palm-sized portion of protein, a modest portion of rice
Mostly chicken, a tiny scoop of rice, no vegetables
Equal parts rice and chicken, no vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: Half vegetables, a palm-sized portion of protein, a modest portion of rice
questions.explanation: Vegetables taking up the largest share, with protein and carbohydrate in reasonable, not dominant, portions, is the balance the plate is built around.
questions.explainWrong: Any plate that leaves out vegetables entirely, or lets rice or chicken take over most of the space, isn't balanced — it's just one food group with a side note.

lessons.title: The Right Amount of Good Fat
lessons.description: A little good fat does more for a dish than cutting out fat entirely.

preparationSteps.title: Measure, don't pour freely
preparationSteps.description: A tablespoon of olive oil carries a salad; a free pour just adds empty calories.

preparationSteps.title: Whole-food fat over processed fat
preparationSteps.description: A few slices of avocado or a spoon of nuts do more nutritionally than the same calories from a processed sauce.

questions.prompt: You're trying to eat lighter but the salad still tastes flat without any fat at all. What's the better fix?
options: Add a measured tablespoon of olive oil or a few slices of avocado
Pour oil freely until it tastes rich
Skip the fat entirely and add more salt instead
Use a bottled low-fat dressing with several added sugars
questions.correctAnswer: Add a measured tablespoon of olive oil or a few slices of avocado
questions.explanation: A small, measured amount of good fat carries flavour without turning the dish into empty calories.
questions.explainWrong: A free pour of oil adds far more calories than the flavour needs, and skipping fat for more salt just trades one problem for another. A bottled low-fat dressing often replaces the fat's flavour with added sugar, which isn't the goal either.

lessons.title: Sweet Without Added Sugar
lessons.description: Ripe fruit, spice and heat can build real sweetness without a bag of sugar.

preparationSteps.title: Use fruit that's properly ripe
preparationSteps.description: Underripe fruit is starchy, not sweet — ripeness does most of the work sugar would otherwise do.

preparationSteps.title: Bake low and slow
preparationSteps.description: Time concentrates the fruit's own sugars as water evaporates out.

preparationSteps.title: Spice instead of sweeten
preparationSteps.description: Cinnamon reads as 'dessert' to the palate without adding a gram of sugar.

questions.prompt: Your baked apple dessert came out bland and starchy instead of sweet, even after baking. What's the likely cause?
options: You didn't add enough cinnamon
The apples weren't ripe enough to begin with
You baked it for too long
You used too much water
questions.correctAnswer: The apples weren't ripe enough to begin with
questions.explanation: Underripe fruit is starchy rather than sweet, and baking concentrates whatever sugars were already there — it can't create sweetness that wasn't present.
questions.explainWrong: Cinnamon adds aroma, not sweetness, so more of it wouldn't fix a starchy result, and neither bake time nor a little extra water changes how ripe the fruit was to start with. Baking only concentrates the sugar that's already there.

lessons.title: One Tray, Whole Dinner
lessons.description: Roasting is the least hands-on way to cook a balanced plate — as long as the oven is hot and the tray isn't crowded.

preparationSteps.title: Preheat properly, 200 °C and up
preparationSteps.description: Food going into a lukewarm oven releases water before it can brown. The tray and the oven both need to be hot first.

preparationSteps.title: One layer, space between pieces
preparationSteps.description: Crowded pieces trap steam and stew. If it doesn't fit in a single layer with gaps, use two trays.

preparationSteps.title: Cut for the cooking time, not for looks
preparationSteps.description: Potatoes go in whole-ish and first, broccoli goes in for the last ten minutes. Same tray, staggered entry.

questions.prompt: Your roast vegetables come out pale, soft and wet instead of browned. The oven was at 200 °C. What went wrong?
options: They needed more oil
The tray was crowded, so they steamed in their own moisture instead of roasting
They needed longer at the same temperature
The oven should have been lower
questions.correctAnswer: The tray was crowded, so they steamed in their own moisture instead of roasting
questions.explanation: Water has to escape for browning to start. Piled-up pieces trap that steam against each other, so they boil in it — no amount of extra time fixes a crowded tray.
questions.explainWrong: Extra oil or extra time on a crowded tray just gives you oilier, softer vegetables, and a lower oven makes the steaming worse. Spread them out or use a second tray.

questions.prompt: Potato and broccoli on the same tray. When does the broccoli go in?
options: At the start, with the potato
In the last ten minutes
Halfway through
On a separate tray at a lower temperature
questions.explanation: Broccoli is done in about ten minutes; potato needs thirty or more. Staggering when each goes in is what lets one tray cook both properly.
questions.explainWrong: Broccoli in from the start or even halfway comes out grey and collapsed by the time the potato is ready, and a second tray at a lower temperature is extra work for a worse result.

lessons.title: Acid, Herb and Heat Instead of Salt
lessons.description: A dish that tastes flat usually isn't short of salt — it's short of acid.

preparationSteps.title: Try acid before more salt
preparationSteps.description: A squeeze of lemon or a splash of vinegar makes a dish taste sharper and fuller. Nine times out of ten that's what 'it needs salt' actually means.

preparationSteps.title: Add herbs off the heat
preparationSteps.description: Dried herbs go in early with the fat; fresh herbs go in at the end, or the heat strips the aroma you added them for.

preparationSteps.title: Let heat and aromatics do the work
preparationSteps.description: Pepper, chilli, garlic and toasted spice give a dish something to notice, which is what salt was being asked to provide.

questions.prompt: A roast tray of vegetables tastes flat. You've already salted it once. What do you reach for first?
options: More salt
A squeeze of lemon or a splash of vinegar
Butter
Sugar
questions.correctAnswer: A squeeze of lemon or a splash of vinegar
questions.explanation: Acid sharpens everything else in the dish, which is the effect people are chasing when they keep adding salt to something already salted.
questions.explainWrong: Doubling the salt on something already salted makes it salty without making it taste less flat, and butter or sugar change the dish into something else instead of lifting what's there.

questions.prompt: When do fresh herbs go in?
options: At the start, so the flavour spreads
Off the heat, at the end
Halfway through cooking
It makes no difference
questions.correctAnswer: Off the heat, at the end
questions.explanation: The volatile aromas that make fresh herbs worth using are driven off by heat — added early, you paid for them and then cooked them away.
questions.explainWrong: Early or halfway, fresh herbs lose exactly the aroma you added them for and turn dark and bitter. Dried herbs are the ones that want the early, long heat.

missions.title: The Balanced Bowl
missions.summary: Steamed vegetables, grilled protein and a modest portion of grain, built in the right proportions.

steps.title: Steam the vegetables
steps.description: Similarly sized pieces, water below the basket, cook until tender with a little bite.

rescues.answer: Still hard after the usual time? Give it a few more minutes — pieces cut too large take longer.
Tender but still with a little bite, bright colour, not mushy.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.description: Season simply and grill until cooked through, without drying it out.

rescues.answer: Looks dry outside but pink inside? Lower the heat and give it a few more minutes covered.

steps.title: Assemble the balanced bowl
steps.description: Half the bowl in vegetables, a palm-sized portion of chicken, a modest portion of rice.

rescues.answer: No brown rice? White rice or another grain works, just adjust the portion the same way.
Vegetables clearly the largest portion, protein and grain in proportion, not overwhelming the plate.

missions.title: Baked Fruit Dessert
missions.summary: Real sweetness from ripe fruit and spice, with a drizzle of good fat to finish.

steps.title: Core and slice the apples
steps.description: Ripe apples, cored and sliced evenly so they bake through at the same rate.

rescues.answer: Apples not quite ripe? Bake a little longer and rely more on the cinnamon and time.

steps.title: Bake low and slow with cinnamon
steps.description: A light dusting of cinnamon, a splash of water in the dish, baked until soft and fragrant.

rescues.answer: Still firm after the usual time? Every oven runs differently — give it more time rather than more heat.
Soft, fragrant, caramelized slightly at the edges, sweet without any added sugar.

steps.title: Finish with a measured touch of fat
steps.description: A few crushed walnuts and a light drizzle of olive oil finish the dish without overloading it.

rescues.answer: No walnuts? Any nut, or a spoon of yoghurt, rounds it out just as well.
A light, measured finish — richer, not greasy.

missions.title: The Balanced Tray
missions.dishName: Sheet-Pan Chicken, Potato and Broccoli, Lemon and Herb
missions.summary: A whole balanced plate out of one tray: protein, starch and vegetable, seasoned with acid rather than salt.

steps.title: Heat the oven and the tray to 200 °C
steps.description: Put the empty tray in while the oven comes up. Food landing on hot metal starts browning immediately instead of sitting in its own water.

rescues.answer: No second tray? Use the largest one you have and plan to cook in two goes.

steps.title: Toss potato and onion, spread in one layer
steps.description: Cut the potatoes into even chunks, toss with a tablespoon of oil, oregano and pepper, and spread them out with gaps between pieces. Roast 20 minutes.

rescues.answer: No oregano? Any dried herb, or just pepper and garlic.
Sticking to the tray? Leave them — they release once the crust forms.

steps.title: Add the chicken, skin up, and roast on
steps.description: Nestle the thighs among the vegetables, skin side up, rubbed with the remaining oil and pepper. Back in for 20 minutes.

rescues.answer: Skin darkening too fast? Drop the oven 20 degrees, don't cover it.
Chickpeas instead of chicken? Drain a can, toss in oil, add them here.

steps.title: Broccoli in for the last ten minutes
steps.description: Break the broccoli into florets, toss in a little oil, and add it to the tray. Ten minutes is enough — you want it green with browned edges, not grey.

rescues.answer: No broccoli? Any quick green: green beans, courgette, peppers.
Tray too full now? Broccoli on a second small tray is fine.

steps.title: Check the chicken is done, then finish with lemon and parsley
steps.description: Juices at the thickest part of the thigh should run clear. Off the heat, squeeze lemon over the whole tray and scatter chopped parsley — and taste before you decide it needs salt.

rescues.answer: Juices clear at the bone, potato browned and tender through, broccoli still green.
No lemon? Vinegar does the same job.
Vegetables darker than you wanted? The lemon and parsley pull it back.
